title: Biu–Mandara languages - Wikipedia
text: The Biu–Mandara or Central Chadic languages of the Afro-Asiatic family are spoken in Nigeria, Chad and Cameroon. A reconstruction of Proto-Central Chadic has been proposed by Gravina (2014).

title: Glavda language - Wikipedia
text: Glavda (also known as Galavda, Gelebda, Glanda, Guelebda, Galvaxdaxa) is an Afro-Asiatic language spoken in Borno State, Nigeria and in Far North Province, Cameroon.

title: Glavda language — Grokipedia
text: Glavda is a Central Chadic language of the Afro-Asiatic family, belonging to the Biu-Mandara subgroup and specifically classified in group A4, spoken by an estimated 20,000 to 40,000 people as of the late 20th century (projected around 40,000 by 1999) primarily in the Gwoza Local Government Area of Borno State, northeastern Nigeria, and in border villages of Cameroon's Far North Province.
